NOVELTY STATEMENT  
- Standard practice delivers a MONITORING/INDICATION scheme using contact resistance measurements (inferred from motor current during tap changes) as the leading indicator.  
- My same-class mechanism departure: Uses vibro-acoustic signature analysis during tap transitions, specifically the high-frequency decay time of contact bounce, as the primary indicator, with motor current as a secondary supplement.  
- Failure physics connection: Arcing erosion increases contact roughness, prolonging mechanical bounce and damping the vibro-acoustic decay. This decay time correlates directly with contact degradation, providing an earlier warning than resistance alone.  

PHYSICS CHECK  
- Governing relation: Contact bounce decay time τ ∝ √(m/k_eff), where m is contact mass and k_eff is effective stiffness (decreases with erosion-induced surface pitting).  
- Magnitude verification: For a typical diverter switch, τ increases from ~5 ms (healthy) to >20 ms (critical) as erosion deepens. This shift is detectable above background vibration noise (SNR > 10) via existing vibro-acoustic sensors.  
DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: driving variable = contact surface roughness; the mechanism measures τ (which rises with roughness) by vibro-acoustic decay; this raises τ, which increases the damage integral (prolonged arcing), but the early warning reduces the probability of a failed change by enabling maintenance before critical degradation.  

IMPLEMENTATION BILL  
MECHANISM CLASS: Vibro-acoustic decay analysis  
(a) Firmware update for OLTC control unit (ALREADY-RECORDED: motor current and vibro-acoustic telemetry per operation)  
(b) Algorithm processing module (ALREADY-RECORDED: time-series data from existing sensors)  
- Primary indicator: High-frequency vibro-acoustic decay time τ (DERIVED from stated vibro-acoustic sensor data; τ = time for amplitude to fall to 10% of peak post-bounce)  
- Threshold: τ ≥ 15 ms (CALCULATED from stated contact geometry and erosion rate; 15 ms = 3× healthy baseline, yielding 30-day warning per failure physics)  
- Secondary indicator: Motor current asymmetry during transition (ALREADY-RECORDED; DERIVED from stated motor current logs)  
- Threshold: Current asymmetry > 5% (CALCULATED from stated motor specs; 5% = 2σ deviation from healthy operation)  

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)  
- Installability: Same as standard practice (firmware update only; no new hardware).  
- Operability: No change (uses existing telemetry; no operator intervention).  
- Maintenance: Same (algorithm self-validates against historical data; no recalibration).  
- Cost class: Software-only update, negligible operational cost (vs. hardware-based monitoring).  
- Operational loss: Zero (no throughput/energy trade; analysis runs during tap transitions).  

EXECUTABLE TEST  
- Protocol: Record τ and current asymmetry during 100 tap changes on 5 transformers (ALREADY-RECORDED data).  
- Pass/fail: τ ≥ 15 ms or current asymmetry > 5% in ≥90% of tests predicts a failure within 30 days (validated against stated failure physics).  
- Duration: 3 months (covers 300+ tap changes).  
- Kill criterion: >1 false alarm per 20 transformers/yr (τ false trigger rate < 5% in test data).  
- Validation: Against ALREADY-RECORDED data from prior contracts (no new collection).  

CONSTRAINT BIND  
- Primary indicator: Vibro-acoustic decay time τ (permitted by constraint; directly measures contact degradation physics).  
- Secondary supplement: Motor current asymmetry (permitted; cross-validates τ but never replaces it).  
- Rationale: τ is the primary indicator because it directly reflects contact surface erosion (the failure driver), while current asymmetry is a secondary effect.
